props.statement: In this case, as shown by (20), the addition of barium carbonate is effective.

props.name: co in feed slightly better kieselguhr
props.statement: Also with the kieselguhr catalyst, results are somewhat better when carbon monoxide is present in the feed.

props.name: co2 28 percent co near 10
props.statement: At 28.4 % CO2 in the feed (run 14, Figure 3) carbon monoxide formation approaches 10 % and the CO2 fraction hardly decreases.

props.name: cu cr hardly usable
props.statement: Cu-Cr catalysts are hardly usable.

props.name: equimolar zn cu 85 percent
props.statement: With the equimolar Zn, Cu catalyst at space velocity 15,300, conversion to methanol reached 85 %, with only slight by-product carbon monoxide and methane (Figure 2).

props.name: equimolar zn cu maximum
props.statement: Comparing (11), (13), (17), (19), (20), (21) and (23), Zn and Cu in equal moles give the highest value; reducing either lowers the reaction rate.

props.name: feed h2 co2 3 to 3.5
props.note: the discussion words it as a proposal (適当であろうと考えられる); the summary (4) states H2:CO2 = 3-3.5:1 as appropriate
props.statement: As feed gas, 25 % CO2 or more is undesirable; somewhat below 25 %, i.e. an H2:CO2 ratio of about 3-3.5:1 by volume, is appropriate.

props.name: high temperature conditions unsuitable
props.statement: Under the conditions of (1)-(10), with about 25 % CO2 in the feed the reaction rate is negligibly low; lowering the CO2 fraction raises it somewhat but side reactions cannot be stopped, and the conditions are unsuitable for recirculation.

props.name: kieselguhr 200atm slight increase
props.statement: With the Mn-Cu catalyst plus 14 % kieselguhr at 200 atm and below 10 % CO2 in the feed, the methanol yield increased somewhat.

props.name: lower temperature by 100C very good
props.statement: Lowering the reaction temperature by about 100 °C relative to (1)-(10) gives very good results.

props.name: methanol analysis methods agree
props.statement: Methanol determined by acetylation (pyridine as auxiliary) and by calculation from the methanol-water specific-gravity table agreed well.

props.name: mn cu kieselguhr too much methane
props.statement: Methane formation is also very large, so from the standpoint of methanol production the Mn-Cu catalyst with kieselguhr is hardly worth considering.

props.name: mn cu scarcely reacts 320 350
props.statement: With the Mn-Cu catalyst at 320-350 °C, 150 atm and space velocity near 4,500 there is almost no reaction, and it tends to produce more methane than carbon monoxide.

props.name: mn cu slight reaction 370 400
props.statement: Raising the temperature to 370-400 °C and lowering the space velocity gives a slight reaction on the Mn-Cu catalyst.

props.name: optimum temperature 250 260
props.note: the discussion says 'seems to be' (思われる); the summary states it; the comparison is with the cited results of Sakikawa et al.
props.statement: For the equimolar Zn, Cu catalyst the optimum reaction temperature, sought in (13)-(16), is 250-260 °C; this is more than 100 °C lower than the optimum (350-400 °C) found by Sakikawa et al.

props.name: recirculation co2 decays co to methane
props.statement: During recirculation (Figure 1, run 10) the amount of carbon dioxide decreases along a logarithmic curve, and carbon monoxide once formed gradually changes to methane; carbon monoxide changes to methane even more than to methanol.

props.name: recirculation increases methanol yield
props.statement: Runs (9) and (10) show that recirculating the gas increases the methanol yield.

props.name: space velocity can be high
props.note: the text layer prints '2$%'; the printed page and Table 1 read 23 % (23.4)
props.statement: Run (12), with only 50 cc of the same catalyst at a space velocity near 60,000, still gave 23 % conversion, showing that the space velocity can be made considerably high.

props.name: summary space velocity 15000
props.note: the comparison is with the cited results of Sakikawa et al.
props.statement: Fully satisfactory results are obtained even at space velocities of 15,000 and above, far larger than the 2,400 that Sakikawa et al. found optimal.

props.name: summary zn cu 50 50 best
props.note: the agreement is with the cited work of Sakikawa et al.
props.statement: Among the catalysts tried, Zn:Cu = 50:50 (mole ratio) gave the best results; this agrees with the results of Sakikawa et al.
